articles.title: Takeaways as Marcus Freeman wraps up Rice & previews Michigan State
articles.summary: Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman spoke to the media on Monday and here are the top takeaways from what he said previewing Michigan State.
articles.body:
Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman met with the media on Monday afternoon , and it seemed like he was pleased with what he saw on Saturday.

The Irish looked dominant in a 52-0 win over visiting Rice , as much of their game was working. Quarterback CJ Carr looked like a star leading the offense, and the defense took advantages of mistakes and started off the scoring.

Freeman spoke on many topics as he wrapped up the Rice game, previewed Michigan State and talked about some areas of improvement. Find out below my top takeaways from Notre Dame's head coach's Monday press conference.

Notre Dame's fundamentals better in Week 2

The scoreboard showed exactly what Freeman was explaining, the fundamentals for the Irish were much better. "We are in a race with every team in the country who can improve faster," he said during his opening comments. It's a unique way of looking at it, not just inside the building but what they'll face as the season continues to advance.

Michigan State will be similar to Northwestern for Notre Dame

Pat Fitzgerald already has made an impact, as he's brought over his winning ways from Northwestern to East Lansing. He's quickly made the Spartans much more competitive, and it will be an interesting challenge for the program.

Notre Dame made late changes to defense vs. Rice, maturity was why

You have a competitive advantage when you have a mature team, as Freeman explained that on Friday, the coaching staff made changes to the game-plan against the Owls. If it wasn't for a mature group, it could have backfired, but the results were stellar. This will surely play as the year goes on, as in crunch time against difficult opponents, the maturity will rise up.

Notre Dame looking to explosive runs, will continue to adjust

It's not just about the players, its about the concepts that the coaches are asking the back to do, which might be a reason why we haven't seen many big runs over the first two games. The leadership and production from last fall is in the NFL, and the coaching might want to take a bit off the backs plate to see more production. It does seem like Jonaz Walton will be getting more touches going forward.

Notre Dame will be smart with Kyngstonn Viliamu-Asa

The star linebacker returned to the field this past weekend, and the impact was huge. Recovering a fumble, near the top of the team lead in tackles, it was a more than impressive 2026 debut. However, Freeman wants to be careful with him, and he's on a snap-count until the medial team fully clears him. Great to see KVA on the field, but there is some caution with him ramping it up too quickly.

Marcus Freeman - 'We are chasing perfection'

Notre Dame wants to be on top of the college football world, and for that, they'll need to collectively be great. Many teams have talked about what Freeman did on Monday, "chasing perfection," and while it was aimed at the wide receivers, you have to believe that its the same mentality for all groups. If the Irish are able to achieve it, a College Football Playoff championship will be the result. I love that this is the goal, as anything less wouldn't unlock the full potential of this team.

articles.body:
See the scenes from Centreville, Constantine and Three Rivers

MARCELLUS — For the second week in a row, a Marcellus football player has earned Footballer of the Week honors.

This week, Blake McWilliams of the Wildcats earned the most votes from area voters. There were 15 student-athletes up for Footballer of the Week honors for the first time since we've been doing this.

McWilliams secured 2,811 total votes. This equated to 37.7 percent of the 7,672 total ballots cast. Xavior Zinsmaster came in second at 1,300 total votes, which was 17.5 percent of the votes.

McWilliams was nominated for the award this week for helping Marcellus move to 2-0 with a victory over Martin last week. He recorded a team-high 15 tackles for Marcellus in the win, plus had an interception and scored a defensive touchdown in the team's 34-23 win. He joined Martelle Enright as Footballer of the Week winners as Enright rushed to the award for the first week of the season.

On Tuesday afternoon, the next installment of the Footballer of the Week poll will be live.

articles.title: Cardiff to host Women’s Champions League final as UEFA reveal 2028 and 2029 venues
articles.summary: Cardiff has been selected to host the UEFA Women’s Champions League final in 2029. The Millenium Stadium, now referred to as the Principality Stadium for spo...
articles.body:
Cardiff has been selected to host the UEFA Women's Champions League final in 2029.

The Millenium Stadium, now referred to as the Principality Stadium for sponsorship reasons, will be the venue for the showpiece event.

It will be the second time the 74,000-capacity ground plays host to a Champions League final after the 2017 men's decider between Real Madrid and Juventus , which was won by the Spanish club. The 2028 final will be played at Lyon 's Parc Olympique Lyonnais.

Cardiff to host Women's Champions League final as UEFA reveal 2028 and 2029 venues

The UEFA Executive Committee also appointed the hosts of several finals at a meeting in Thessaloniki in Greece on Tuesday, including the 2028 and 2029 men's Champions League finals.

The 2028 edition will take place at the Allianz Arena in Munich, while Barcelona 's new Camp Nou will host the final for the first time since its revamp the following year.

Bayern 's home stadium has hosted the final twice previously in 2012 and 2025, while Barcelona last did so in 1999 when Sir Alex Ferguson's Manchester United won the competition for a second time in their history.

Meanwhile, UEFA also decided that the 2028 and 2029 UEFA Europa League finals will be hosted by Bucharest, Romania and Belgrade, Serbia respectively.

Juventus ' Allianz Stadium will host the UEFA Conference League final in 2028 and the following year's final will be take place at the Puskas Arena in Budapest.

Next year's UEFA Super Cup will be played at Ajax 's Johan Cruyff Arena in Amsterdam, while the 2028 edition will be taken all the way to Kazakhstan, with the final between the Champions League and Europa League winners taking place at the Astana Arena.

List of venues appointed by UEFA on Tuesday:

2028: Parc Olympic Lyonnais, Lyon-Décines

2029: National Stadium of Wales, Cardiff

articles.title: Why has Dino Toppmöller been sacked by RC Lens?
articles.summary: The news came as a real blow. Barely three months after taking over from Pierre Sage as manager of RC Lens, Dino Toppmöller is reportedly on the verge of bei...
articles.body:
The news came as a real blow. Barely three months after taking over from Pierre Sage as manager of RC Lens , Dino Toppmöller is reportedly on the verge of being sacked.

This decision by the club's board inevitably raises questions, given that the German manager has only been in charge of six matches this season – one of which led to victory for Les Sang et Or in the Trophée des Champions and another to a stunning win in the Champions League.

And whilst things have not been perfect in recent weeks – particularly in terms of performances and results in Ligue 1 (Lens have won just one of their first four league matches) – few, from the outside at least, could have imagined the situation escalating to such an extent.

In this light, it comes as no surprise that sporting performance was not the primary reason for Toppmöller's dismissal. Indeed, according to reports from Sky Sport Deutschland , the decision stemmed instead from the German coach's loyalty to his assistant, Nelson Morgado, himself on the verge of being sacked by the Lens management.

Regarded internally as a disruptive figure, Morgado is said to have come under fire for the high standards he demanded of the French coaching staff in terms of commitment, passion and energy. Toppmöller, who opposed his superiors' decision, is said to have, for his part, given his colleague his unwavering support, thereby bringing about his own dismissal. Even though he was held in high regard by his superiors.
